primary.rule: search_plan mean lines > tetris_plan mean lines

secondary.rule: search_plan Tetris line rate >= tetris_plan Tetris line rate

conclusion: search_plan beat the unchanged tetris_plan on mean lines over the held-out seeds and the experiment's primary acceptance holds

decision_budget.note: One row per configured (agent, seed); decisions and nodes_expanded are deterministic and a fresh run reproduces them, while episode_seconds is measured on the reporting machine and is not reproducible across machines. The search is capped by the integer node budget, never by a wall clock.

engine_dependency.statement: the reported rows reproduce only with this Block Stack working tree; its uncommitted local changes cannot be exported and are not retained here, so the engine source is identified but not reconstructable

limitations: The sibling engine is a read-only registered dependency. Its working tree is dirty, the uncommitted changes cannot be exported from this repository and are not retained, so the rows are identified but not reconstructable from the engine commit alone.
The search's wall-clock seconds are measured on the machine that ran the evaluation; only the deterministic decision and node counts are reproducible.

The stock `block-stack-ai verify` command cannot verify a search record, because the record's objective sources deliberately include the well plan dependency the stock walk excludes; use `python -m block_stack_ai.experiment005 verify`.

leaf_weights.tie_break: first highest-valued placement in canonical enumeration order: orientation ascending, then column ascending

weights.tie_break: highest searched value; ties keep the first placement in canonical enumeration order (orientation ascending, then column ascending)

acceptance.primary: search_plan's mean lines over the held-out seeds is greater than tetris_plan's mean lines over the same seeds, both re-measured by this experiment with the pinned engine
acceptance.report_only: lookahead's mean lines, mean score and Tetris line rate are reported for context and carry no acceptance threshold
acceptance.secondary: search_plan's Tetris line rate is at least tetris_plan's on the same seeds

leaf_weights.tie_break: first highest-valued placement in canonical enumeration order: orientation ascending, then column ascending

weights.tie_break: highest searched value; ties keep the first placement in canonical enumeration order (orientation ascending, then column ascending)

question: Does a deterministic, player-visible search one piece deeper than Experiment 004's preview, over plausible unseen pieces and reusing 004's well-plan leaf, beat the unchanged 004 plan and the plain lookahead on held-out seeds?

seed_protocol.identity: SHA256 of sorted compact JSON of the complete native State dataclass, with only the seed field removed
seed_protocol.selection: SHA256(fallgorithm005/review-holdout/v1/<index>), first two bytes big-endian; skip native-state collisions; no gameplay outcomes inspected
